output:
**Subject: The building on Saint-Hubert**

Denis,

I am writing because I am too angry to have this conversation properly right now. I need you to read this all the way through, and then I need you to call me.

On Thursday morning at six, I was in the bakery shaping baguettes when a photographer from the real estate agency came in. A stranger with a camera, in my shop, while I was working. He told me that you had said I was okay with it.

I was not okay with it. I did not even know the building was being put on the market.

Karine had to calm me down. Think about that for a minute: my employee had to calm me down because this is how I found out what my own brother was doing. Afterwards I found the listing on Centris, at $1,150,000. You could arrange an agent, a listing and a photographer, but you could not call me yourself.

I am furious, Denis. Not only because you are trying to sell the building, but because you went behind my back and let me hear about it from a stranger. And you told that stranger I had agreed. I want to know why.

After Maman’s funeral, you called me and said, “No rush, we decide together.” I remember those words. Together. Since her death in February, and since the estate was settled in August, the building has belonged half to you and half to me. When did “together” become making these arrangements without even telling me?

This is Papa’s building on rue Saint-Hubert. He bought it in 1979. There is the bakery downstairs and the two apartments upstairs. You know every corner of it. Do you remember how Papa used to let you sleep in the room at the back with the flour sacks? You loved it in there. I keep thinking about that little boy and wondering how we arrived at a stranger walking into the bakery with a camera.

Maybe you think I am being sentimental. Of course I am. It was Papa’s building, and we have just lost Maman. But this is business too. My bakery has been there for 31 years. I have six employees who depend on this business and customers who have been coming through that door for years. This is not simply a property listing to me. It is my work, my livelihood, and a place other people count on.

I have paid $2,400 a month in rent to the estate and I have never been late, not once. In 2019, I paid $38,000 for the new roof myself. I am not saying that settles everything between us, but it is part of the history of this building and needs to be part of our discussion.

My lease ends on April 30, 2027. If the building is sold, I do not know what a new owner will want to do. I am frightened that a developer could tear it down or turn it into condos, or that my rent could double. I cannot survive that. You live in Calgary, so perhaps it is harder to see what this means here, every morning, for me and for the people who work with me. But I need you to try.

I already told you in September, on the phone, that I want to buy your half. The caisse has pre-approved me for $410,000. I know we may not agree on the value, and I am not pretending that pre-approval answers every question. But I made you an offer because I want us to find a way forward. If you think it is not enough, then tell me that. Talk to me. We can look at the numbers, including what I paid for the roof, and see whether there is a fair arrangement we can both accept.

What I am asking is this: **take the building off the market this week so we can discuss my buying your half.** At the very least, give me the first opportunity to buy before you go any further with a sale. Please also tell the agent not to send anyone else into the bakery without speaking to me first. I cannot have people appearing during the working day because they were told I had agreed to something I knew nothing about.

I know you have your own reasons and your own plans. I am willing to hear them. You are my brother, and your share matters too. But I need you to understand how deeply hurtful this has been. You did not just surprise me with a business decision. You made me feel that my years of work there, and your promise that we would decide together, counted for nothing.

I do not want to lose the bakery, and I do not want to lose you over this either. That is why I am writing instead of saying some of the things I wanted to say when I saw that listing. I am still angry, and I expect an honest explanation. But I want us to find a solution we can live with.

Please call me yourself this week. I want to hear your voice and speak to you directly, not receive an answer by text from your wife. Tell me what is happening with the listing and whether you will pause it so we can sit down and talk about my offer.

We have already lost too much this year. Please do not let this be the way we treat each other now.

Your sister
